findings.text: There was no stone here, only cobbles and thatch, and the horses telling her what her hand could not.
findings.reason: 'no X, only Y' minimizer. Deletion test passes: the previous sentence already sets the stone-reading limit, so the positive half carries it.
findings.suggestedFix: Here there were only cobbles and thatch, and the horses telling her what her hand could not.
findings.deletionTest: Only cobbles and thatch here, and the horses telling her what her hand could not.

findings.text: He had not dropped it.
findings.reason: Preamble negation. 'laid the knife down straight, the way a man lays down a tool he means to pick up again' in the next sentence already makes the dropped/laid-down distinction. Part of a 3-kill cluster (L51/L63/L69). Fix is deletion: the paragraph opens on 'He had stopped in the middle of a spoke'.
findings.deletionTest: He had stopped in the middle of a spoke ... and laid the knife down straight ...

findings.text: The next house had no supper on the table, only a porridge pot by the hearth with a crust dried on it and one bowl scraped clean, the beds not made at all.
findings.reason: 'no supper ..., only a porridge pot' bats one meal away to land on another. The porridge already marks a breakfast house. Part of the L49-L69 cluster.
findings.suggestedFix: In the next house a porridge pot stood by the hearth with a crust dried on it, one bowl scraped clean beside it, the beds unmade.
findings.deletionTest: The next house had only a porridge pot by the hearth ...

findings.text: This village had not been sacked.
findings.reason: Preamble negation after the Amani sentence has already set out what a sacked steading looks like. Fix is deletion, applied together with A-I02, which rewrites the next sentence. Part of the L49-L69 cluster.
findings.deletionTest: (Amani sentence) + It had stopped, one house at breakfast ...

findings.text: "Not the worst. Down by the mill."
findings.reason: Dialogue fragment pivot of the same shape as the calibration KILL 'Not strongest here. Just everywhere.' A positive comparative gives the same ranking.
findings.suggestedFix: "Worse again down by the mill."
findings.deletionTest: Worse than the well. Down by the mill.

findings.text: She was asking, not arguing.
findings.reason: 'X, not Y' tone tag. The rejected half 'arguing' is never acted on, so it is not a binary diagnostic.
findings.suggestedFix: She was asking.

findings.text: Not loud. Neral never said anything loud.
findings.reason: Two stacked negations about volume. The line 'Then, after a moment, in exactly the same voice' already carries Neral's calm. Fix is deletion: the paragraph opens on '"Ranger-General." Then, after a moment, ...', and the previous paragraph ('when Neral said her name through the wall') attributes it.
findings.deletionTest: "Ranger-General." Then, after a moment, in exactly the same voice ...

findings.text: The words did not matter; it was the sound that went down through the cracks, warm and unhurried.
findings.reason: 'not X; it was Y' pivot. Starting at Y keeps everything.

findings.deletionTest: The sound went down through the cracks, warm and unhurried.

findings.text: No more than that.
findings.reason: Minimizer fragment. 'It's in the ground, the same as everywhere' already states the baseline level, and the next line makes the diagnostic. Fix is deletion.
findings.deletionTest: It's in the ground, the same as everywhere. Nothing that's been in here was carrying it.

findings.text: It was not a soft question, for all the voice was soft.
findings.reason: Rejects a descriptor to imply its opposite. Name the descriptor.
findings.suggestedFix: It was a hard question, for all the voice was soft.

findings.text: Cyndia's voice did not go up. It went, if anything, a little lower and more careful.
findings.reason: Preamble negation that primes a rise so the real reaction lands. The deletion test passes cleanly.

findings.text: Not stars.

repeatNouns: the village (L69 stopped, L103 gave/kept, L587 kept, L591 held)
audits.secondSweep: Dedicated P5/P6 sweep: re-read every sentence for an inanimate or abstract subject carrying agency, cognition or physical-behaviour verbs. It added A-I05 (terror 'come up with'), A-I06 (the day 'folded over on itself'), A-I14 (the ditch 'had had them') and A-I15 (legs 'sure of her'). It confirmed the village metaphor chain across L69/L103/L587/L591. Roads and geography ('the road climbed', 'It ran north', 'the road came round the shoulder') stay as literal 'the road led' uses. No plans, maps or answers carry revision verbs. Body-part subjects were all checked, and only those whose involuntariness is the point (arm flinched, fingers would not close, head jerking down asleep, ears reddening) were kept.

findings.text: Her left hand came up off the stirrup, palm out, beginning some shape she meant to draw in the air for the slow soldier. It stopped there and went back down.
findings.reason: Across two sentences the hand carries the mage's aborted decision. The next sentence names the decision as hers ('watch her decide not to argue'). With the mage as subject, the meaning is unchanged.
findings.suggestedFix: She brought her left hand up off the stirrup, palm out, to begin some shape in the air for the slow soldier, then stopped and put it back down.
findings.subject: her left hand / it
findings.verb: came up ... beginning ... stopped ... went back down
findings.realAgent: the mage, choosing not to argue

findings.text: It had stopped, one house at breakfast and the next at supper and the next at a sickbed, as if everybody had got up from what they were doing at a different hour of a different day and gone out of the door and shut it.
findings.reason: 'The village' is the subject of human verbs four times in the chapter (stopped L69, gave/kept L103, kept L587, held L591). Under the repeat-noun cluster rule every instance is a KILL. The real actors, 'everybody', are already inside this sentence, so put them in subject position. Apply with A-N04 (delete the preceding sentence).
findings.suggestedFix: Here everybody had got up from what they were doing, one house at breakfast and the next at supper and the next at a sickbed, each at a different hour of a different day, and gone out of the door and shut it.
findings.subject: the village (It)

findings.text: Her hand was on the string before she knew it.
findings.reason: Matches the calibration KILL 'Her fingers found the bowstring before she had decided to reach for it.' The involuntary-hand beat comes back at L355 and L599. L599 is the deliberate exhausted echo, so the first instance gives up the 'before she knew it' wrapper. 'She eased the string.' still follows cleanly.
findings.suggestedFix: She had the string half-drawn.
findings.subject: her hand
findings.verb: was on the string before she knew it

findings.text: The village had given her its tables and its pegs and a cat. It had kept the rest.
findings.reason: The village is given 'given' and 'kept', which are verbs of deliberate withholding. The real agents are the rangers who swept and the villagers who left these things behind. This is a repeat-noun instance.
findings.suggestedFix: Both sides swept, and all they had to show for it was tables and pegs and a cat.

findings.realAgent: the sweep (Sylvanas, Cyndia, Lyriel) and what the departed villagers left

findings.text: A child's terror didn't come up with a shaving glass.
findings.reason: The abstraction 'terror' is the subject of an invention verb. The real agent is the child. The negation itself stays, as a kept binary diagnostic of the witness's credibility.
findings.suggestedFix: A frightened child didn't make up a shaving glass.

findings.text: The day had gone on so long it had folded over on itself.
findings.reason: The abstraction 'the day' gets a reflexive physical action. The real source is Sylvanas's sleeplessness, which L21 established. The fix ties it to the afternoon event in the same paragraph.

findings.subject: the day
findings.realAgent: Sylvanas's fatigue and lost sense of time

findings.text: the one sound the village had kept
findings.reason: The village 'kept' a sound. This is the third village retention verb and a repeat-noun instance. What is actually there: the race runs on because nobody is left to make other noise.
